```{r}
#| label: load-data
documents <- read.csv("data/agora/documents.csv")
authorities <- read.csv("data/agora/authorities.csv")
```

## Research question and hypotheses

Does who issues an AI policy affect whether it gets enacted?

**Hypothesis (H1):** AI policies issued by federal agencies are more likely to be enacted than AI bills proposed in Congress.

**Null hypothesis (H0):** The issuing authority makes no difference to whether an AI policy is enacted.

In this AGORA extract, four agency AI rows have `Most.recent.activity` Defunct and a 2025 activity date, including the 2023 AI executive order.

[fill in later]

## Data

The data are AGORA v1.32.0, the AI GOvernance and Regulatory Archive from the Emerging Technology Observatory (ETO) at Georgetown. I use `documents.csv` and `authorities.csv`. Each row is one AGORA document. Big laws are split by AI section, so Congress has 364 rows from 177 bills.

I keep US Congress, federal agencies and states. That is 1,126 of 1,251 rows. I drop Defunct, because the outcome is enacted or proposed. That leaves N = 706 (2017 to 2026). Treatment is federal agency (53) versus Congress (364). States (289) are context only. I do not add controls in the main comparison.

## A first look at the data

```{r}
#| label: first-look
head(documents[, c("Authority", "Most.recent.activity")])
dim(documents)
dim(authorities)

## View(documents)

## most recent activity
table(documents$Most.recent.activity, exclude = NULL)

## number of different authorities
dim(table(documents$Authority))
```

## Coding the issuer

I match each document's authority to `Parent.authority` in `authorities.csv`. Congress is the United States Congress. Federal agencies are the other authorities whose parent is "Federal government". States have parent "State governments". Everything else is dropped (other countries, cities, and so on).

```{r}
#| label: parent-group
## parent group for each authority (from authorities.csv)
documents$parent <- authorities$Parent.authority[match(documents$Authority,
                                                       authorities$Name)]
sum(is.na(match(documents$Authority, authorities$Name)))
table(documents$parent, exclude = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: issuer
## issuer: Congress, federal agency or state
documents$issuer <- NA
documents$issuer <- ifelse(documents$Authority == "United States Congress",
                           "Congress", documents$issuer)
documents$issuer <- ifelse(documents$parent == "Federal government" &
                           documents$Authority != "United States Congress",
                           "Federal agency", documents$issuer)
documents$issuer <- ifelse(documents$parent == "State governments",
                           "State", documents$issuer)
table(documents$issuer, exclude = NULL)

## authorities counted as federal agencies
table(documents$Authority[documents$issuer == "Federal agency"])
```

## Proposed and enacted

I keep Congress, federal agencies and states, then drop Defunct. The outcome `enacted` is 1 if Most recent activity is Enacted, and 0 if Proposed.

```{r}
#| label: dropping-defunct
## keeping Congress, federal agencies and states only
issuers <- documents[!is.na(documents$issuer), ]
table(issuers$issuer, issuers$Most.recent.activity)

## dropping Defunct (DV is proposed or enacted)
policies <- issuers[issuers$Most.recent.activity != "Defunct", ]
policies$enacted <- ifelse(policies$Most.recent.activity == "Enacted", 1, 0)

## N used and dropped
nrow(documents)
nrow(documents) - nrow(issuers)
sum(issuers$Most.recent.activity == "Defunct")
nrow(policies)
```

## Enacted by issuer

Share enacted in the main sample: federal agency 90.56604%, Congress 53.84615%, state 75.43253%.

```{r}
#| label: activity-counts
## enacted and proposed by issuer
activity_counts <- table(policies$issuer, policies$Most.recent.activity)
activity_counts
sum(activity_counts)

## percentages within each issuer
100 * prop.table(activity_counts, margin = 1)

## share enacted by issuer
congress <- policies$enacted[policies$issuer == "Congress"]
agency <- policies$enacted[policies$issuer == "Federal agency"]
state <- policies$enacted[policies$issuer == "State"]

table(policies$issuer)

pct_enacted <- 100 * c("Congress" = mean(congress),
                       "Federal agency" = mean(agency),
                       "State" = mean(state))
pct_enacted
```

```{r}
#| label: group-intervals
## 95% confidence intervals
## Congress
100 * (mean(congress) - 1.96 * sqrt(var(congress) / length(congress)))
100 * (mean(congress) + 1.96 * sqrt(var(congress) / length(congress)))

## federal agency
100 * (mean(agency) - 1.96 * sqrt(var(agency) / length(agency)))
100 * (mean(agency) + 1.96 * sqrt(var(agency) / length(agency)))

## state
100 * (mean(state) - 1.96 * sqrt(var(state) / length(state)))
100 * (mean(state) + 1.96 * sqrt(var(state) / length(state)))
```

## Federal agency vs Congress

I compare mean(agency `enacted`) with mean(Congress `enacted`). The difference is 36.71988 points (95% CI 27.26362 to 46.17615). z = 7.610931. Two-sided p = 2.721295e-14. `2 * pnorm(-abs(z_obs)) < 0.05` is TRUE. Rounded: 36.7 (27.3 to 46.2). `lm(enacted ~ agency)` gives the same slope, 0.3671988. t = 5.220443. p = 2.827761e-07.

[fill in later]

```{r}
#| label: difference-in-means
## federal agency vs Congress
treatment <- policies[policies$issuer == "Federal agency", ]
control <- policies[policies$issuer == "Congress", ]
n_t <- nrow(treatment)
n_c <- nrow(control)

## difference in means
diff_means <- mean(treatment$enacted) - mean(control$enacted)
100 * diff_means

## standard error
se_diff <- sqrt(var(treatment$enacted) / n_t + var(control$enacted) / n_c)

## 95% confidence interval
100 * (diff_means - 1.96 * se_diff)
100 * (diff_means + 1.96 * se_diff)

## z-statistic and p-values
z_obs <- diff_means / se_diff
z_obs
2 * pnorm(-abs(z_obs))
pnorm(-z_obs)

## reject H0 at 5%?
2 * pnorm(-abs(z_obs)) < 0.05
```

```{r}
#| label: regression
## same comparison with lm()
two_groups <- policies[policies$issuer != "State", ]
two_groups$agency <- ifelse(two_groups$issuer == "Federal agency", 1, 0)
fit <- lm(enacted ~ agency, data = two_groups)
fit
summary(fit)$coef
```

## Checks

I run five checks.

- Defunct counted as not enacted: agency n = 57, Congress n = 735; difference 57.54386 points; 95% CI 47.47171 to 67.61601; z = 11.1978; p = 4.17978e-29.
- Without the Executive Office of the President: agency n = 35; difference 37.58242 points; 95% CI 26.86577 to 48.29907; z = 6.873559; p = 6.261965e-12.
- Validated rows only (`Validated. == "true"`): Congress Enacted 159, Proposed 1; federal agency Enacted 25, Proposed 1; agency n = 26, Congress n = 160; difference −3.221154 points; 95% CI −10.8585 to 4.41619; z = −0.8266567; p = 0.4084317.
- Without NDAA rows (`NDAA` in `Collections`): NDAA rows are Congress 148, agency 0, state 0; Congress without NDAA n = 216, enacted share 22.22222%; difference 68.34382 points; 95% CI 58.6483 to 78.03933; z = 13.81607; p = 2.039083e-43.
- `lm(enacted ~ agency + applies_gov)`: `agency` 0.4923000 (SE 0.04458397, t = 11.042085, p = 5.073422e-25); `applies_gov` 0.7492864 (SE 0.02980550, t = 25.139196, p = 2.397216e-85).

```{r}
#| label: check-defunct
## check 1: Defunct counted as not enacted
issuers$enacted <- ifelse(issuers$Most.recent.activity == "Enacted", 1, 0)
agency_all <- issuers$enacted[issuers$issuer == "Federal agency"]
congress_all <- issuers$enacted[issuers$issuer == "Congress"]
length(agency_all)
length(congress_all)

diff_defunct <- mean(agency_all) - mean(congress_all)
se_defunct <- sqrt(var(agency_all) / length(agency_all) +
                   var(congress_all) / length(congress_all))
100 * diff_defunct
100 * (diff_defunct - 1.96 * se_defunct)
100 * (diff_defunct + 1.96 * se_defunct)
diff_defunct / se_defunct
2 * pnorm(-abs(diff_defunct / se_defunct))
```

```{r}
#| label: check-no-eop
## check 2: without the Executive Office of the President
agency_no_eop <- policies$enacted[policies$issuer == "Federal agency" &
                                  policies$Authority != "Executive Office of the President"]
length(agency_no_eop)

diff_no_eop <- mean(agency_no_eop) - mean(control$enacted)
se_no_eop <- sqrt(var(agency_no_eop) / length(agency_no_eop) +
                  var(control$enacted) / n_c)
100 * diff_no_eop
100 * (diff_no_eop - 1.96 * se_no_eop)
100 * (diff_no_eop + 1.96 * se_no_eop)
diff_no_eop / se_no_eop
2 * pnorm(-abs(diff_no_eop / se_no_eop))
```

```{r}
#| label: check-validated
## check 3: validated rows only
validated <- policies[policies$Validated. == "true", ]
table(validated$issuer, validated$Most.recent.activity)

agency_val <- validated$enacted[validated$issuer == "Federal agency"]
congress_val <- validated$enacted[validated$issuer == "Congress"]
length(agency_val)
length(congress_val)

diff_val <- mean(agency_val) - mean(congress_val)
se_val <- sqrt(var(agency_val) / length(agency_val) +
               var(congress_val) / length(congress_val))
100 * diff_val
100 * (diff_val - 1.96 * se_val)
100 * (diff_val + 1.96 * se_val)
diff_val / se_val
2 * pnorm(-abs(diff_val / se_val))
```

```{r}
#| label: check-ndaa
## check 4: without the NDAA rows
policies$ndaa <- ifelse(grepl("NDAA", policies$Collections), 1, 0)
table(policies$issuer, policies$ndaa)

congress_no_ndaa <- policies$enacted[policies$issuer == "Congress" &
                                     policies$ndaa == 0]
length(congress_no_ndaa)
100 * mean(congress_no_ndaa)

diff_no_ndaa <- mean(agency) - mean(congress_no_ndaa)
se_no_ndaa <- sqrt(var(agency) / length(agency) +
                   var(congress_no_ndaa) / length(congress_no_ndaa))
100 * diff_no_ndaa
100 * (diff_no_ndaa - 1.96 * se_no_ndaa)
100 * (diff_no_ndaa + 1.96 * se_no_ndaa)
diff_no_ndaa / se_no_ndaa
2 * pnorm(-abs(diff_no_ndaa / se_no_ndaa))
```

```{r}
#| label: check-applies-gov
## check 5: lm() also holding constant whether the policy mainly applies to government
two_groups$applies_gov <- ifelse(two_groups$Primarily.applies.to.the.government == "true", 1, 0)
table(two_groups$issuer, two_groups$applies_gov)

fit_gov <- lm(enacted ~ agency + applies_gov, data = two_groups)
fit_gov
summary(fit_gov)$coef
```

## Text analysis

I split the short summaries in `analysis.R`. Tokens are letters only and at least 3 characters. I drop the stop, month, drafting and US state list in `stops`. Each issuer is one bag of words. tf-idf is (count / issuer total) times log(3 / how many issuers use the word). The tables print from `analysis.R`.

Token totals: Congress 8,258, federal agency 1,366, state 7,031. Highest tf-idf, Congress: director 0.005587517, congressional 0.003059831, navy 0.002261614, guard 0.001995542, coast 0.001862506. Highest tf-idf, agency: efficacy, hazard, icts, ideological, labeling, rate each 0.003217020. Highest tf-idf, state: sexual 0.002343790, generative 0.002133723, media 0.002133723. Word-share correlation, Congress vs agency: 0.4242353 (480 shared words). Congress vs state: 0.4558262 (917 shared words).

## Limitations

Issuers were not randomly assigned. Congress has 177 unique `Link.to.document` values among 364 rows. 318 of 706 `policies` rows have `Summaries.and.tags.may.include.unreviewed.machine.output == "true"`. Agency n = 53.
